parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, facility ban, border or detention rule, or documented police targeting is recorded; same-sex conduct under Section 164 was decriminalised by courts in 2019/2021 and formally deleted in 2026, with functioning courts ordering gender recognition for residents. Counterweights are only moderate social tolerance (50% in 2021 re homosexual neighbour, not trans-specific), recorded societal discrimination, mixed official rhetoric, unsatisfactory implementation of precedents, and no documented visitor-facing remedies for facilities, custody or care. Section 167 status remains uncertain and is a secondary sexuality-law factor. This sits in reduced risk, above repeated visitor-facing harm, below documented acceptance plus working visitor remedies.

entry_documents.interaction: No evidence foreign passports or markers are challenged; resident litigation-only marker change does not reach visitor documents.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented stops, detention placement, searches or custody abuse for trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No birth-sex facility rule is recorded at any level, but identity-based access is also not documented.

care_services.interaction: Emergency ward placement and medication access for visitors are unresolved in the dossier.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Mixed official signals, including a 2011 deputy speaker remark about killing gay people, alongside presidents condemning hate speech and acknowledging discrimination; Section 167 status unresolved.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Section 164 decriminalised 2019, upheld 2021, deleted 2026; courts protected dignity, privacy and expression in 2017 gender-recognition cases.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law is secondary; no documented use against visibly gender-nonconforming visitors, and prosecutions before 2019 were rare.

minors_guardians.interaction: No partnership recognition affects resident couples; no traveller-facing minor, guardianship or family-visit rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2011 report found no reported violence based on sexual orientation or gender identity that year; societal discrimination was recorded. No later data.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Courts and community organisation provide public legal resources; enforcement outcomes for visitor assaults are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of recent violence data in a thin record is not evidence of safety, and tolerance data concern homosexual neighbours, not trans people.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: May 2024 assessment: implementation of landmark precedents has not been satisfactory; no administrative gender-recognition process as of 2023 review.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2016 registration order for leading LGBTIQ+ organisation operating advocacy and support; repeated court victories show recourse can work.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident remedies demonstrate functioning courts but do not document a working visitor-facing hotels, facilities or border remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: no trans offence or targeting, community infrastructure and court recourse, but only friction/awkwardness and open custody questions. This dossier has stronger court decriminalisation and registration, yet weaker documented social acceptance of trans people, so not materially above 0.65.

Higher safety than this case: documented identity-based facilities, enforced court compensation for a traveller, and established community respect. None of those visitor-facing protections is documented here, placing this below 0.75.

Much safer than 0.35: there is no birth-sex public-building rule, document checks, or rejected complaints confirming exclusion. The worst documented features are social discrimination and implementation gaps, not a universal unremedied exposure.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is nationally uniform with no documented subnational layer. Decriminalisation and court-ordered recognition make state persecution unlikely, and a registered community organisation plus functioning courts provide some recourse. However, visitor journey stages—entry, facilities, custody, care—are undocumented rather than proven safe, violence data are dated to 2011, and tolerance is only 50% for a different population. Uncertain Section 167 does not dominate. Net effect: reduced risk around 0.65, limited by lack of documented acceptance and operating visitor remedies.
